Empirical Research Plan

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Strategy: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) event-study with matched controls.

Rationale  
• “Treatment” (SEC targeting for misrepresentation) is a discrete, well-timed shock whose first public disclosure date is known.  
• For each treated firm we can find an ex-ante similar firm that was not targeted (matched on 2-digit SIC, size, fiscal year, profitability, leverage).  
• Stock-market, regulatory, and litigation outcomes can be observed both before and after the disclosure, allowing us to compare pre/post changes between treated and control firms.  
• A DiD event-study (firm × day panel) nets out market-wide shocks and common industry/size trends.  
• The same DiD framework can be extended to dollar penalties, class-action settlements, and longer-run operating performance to compute the “total cost.”

Why not event study alone?  A pure abnormal-return study captures valuation effects but cannot disentangle contemporaneous shocks common to all firms; DiD adds a credible counterfactual.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Treatment variable  
Treatment_it = 1 for firm i on all days t ≥ τ_i , where τ_i is the first public announcement date of the misconduct (initial restatement or first SEC investigation announcement).

Control group  
For every treated firm, one (or several) matched non-target firm(s) in the same fiscal year that:  
• share the same 2-digit SIC,  
• are in the same NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ listing tier,  
• have total assets within the nearest decile,  
• have similar leverage and ROA (Mahalanobis or propensity-score distance),  
and never receive an AAER over the sample period.

Timing / variation  
Identification comes from the differential change in outcomes starting at τ_i for treated versus control firms. Robustness: shift τ_i by ±5 trading days, or use the final SEC order date instead of the initial announcement.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Parallel trends. Absent enforcement, treated and matched control firms would have experienced the same evolution in returns, penalties (zero), and operating performance.  
Plausibility: Matching on industry, size, and performance helps; we will test pre-trend equivalence in a ±250-day pre-period.

A2. No differential anticipation. Investors in control firms should not anticipate enforcement against those firms, and investors in treated firms should not receive major leakage more than (say) 30 trading days before τ_i.  
Plausibility: SEC investigations are typically non-public until announced; we will test for return drifts pre-τ_i.

A3. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA). One firm’s targeting does not directly affect another matched firm’s outcomes.  
Plausibility: Firms seldom compete head-to-head at the 2-digit SIC level; we will drop pairs within the same four-digit SIC when evaluating operating outcomes.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Imperfect matching / remaining selection bias.  
Remedy: (i) Propensity-score weighting; (ii) firm-fixed effects in panel; (iii) covariate-adjusted DiD.

T2. Information leakage or rumors pre-τ_i.  
Remedy: (i) Conduct placebo tests in the ‑60 to ‑10 window; (ii) re-estimate excluding firms with abnormal volume spikes or newspaper coverage pre-event.

T3. Spillovers (industry contagion).  
Remedy: (i) Include industry-day fixed effects in daily return regressions; (ii) cluster standard errors at the industry level; (iii) re-estimate after dropping all firms in the same 3-digit SIC that also announce restatements within ±30 days.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# ‑-- Packages ‑--
library(data.table); library(lubridate); library(fixest); library(did)
library(xts); library(PerformanceAnalytics)

# 1. Data Loading
aaer  <- fread("aaer.csv")        # firm_id, event_date, penalties, etc.
crsp  <- fread("crsp_daily.csv")  # firm_id, date, ret, mkt_ret
comp  <- fread("compustat.csv")   # firm_id, fyear, at, roa, lev

# 2. Merge & Construct Variables
aaer[, event_date := as.Date(event_date)]
crsp[, date := as.Date(date)]

# (a) Identify controls (simple Mahalanobis match)
pre_vars <- c("sic2","size_rank","roa","lev")
treated  <- unique(aaer$firm_id)
controls <- match_controls(treated, comp, pre_vars)   # user-defined function

# (b) Flag treatment in daily panel
panel <- rbind(crsp[firm_id %in% treated],
               crsp[firm_id %in% controls])
panel <- merge(panel, aaer[,.(firm_id, event_date)], by="firm_id", all.x=TRUE)
panel[, post := ifelse(date >= event_date, 1, 0)]
panel[, treat := ifelse(firm_id %in% treated, 1, 0)]
panel[, treat_post := treat*post]

# (c) Excess return (market-adjusted)
panel[, excess_ret := ret - mkt_ret]

# 3. Main DiD Regression (daily returns)
reg1 <- feols(excess_ret ~ treat_post | firm_id + date, data=panel,
              cluster = ~ sic2)
summary(reg1)

# Convert coefficient to dollar loss
coef <- coef(reg1)["treat_post"]
avg_mktcap <- panel[date == (event_date-1), mean(mktcap, na.rm=TRUE)]
dollar_loss <- coef * avg_mktcap * 3  # assume CAR-3,+3 window

# 4. Reputational Cost = Market loss ‑ (civil + class + criminal)
aaer_tot <- aaer[, .(pen = civil_penalty + class_settle + criminal_fine),
                 by=firm_id]
reput <- dollar_loss - aaer_tot$pen

# 5. Robustness: event-study plot
es <- did::att_gt(yname="excess_ret", tname="date", idname="firm_id",
                  gname="event_date", data=panel, allow_unbalanced_panel=TRUE)
did::ggdid(es)
```
(NB: `match_controls` is a placeholder; in practice use `MatchIt` or `optmatch`.)

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Direction: Negative abnormal returns around first announcement; positive coefficients for penalties in dollar terms.  
Magnitude (prior): Cumulative abnormal return of −15 % (median) over [-1,+1], roughly 6-8 × reported overstatement; direct cash penalties ~5 % of the total market loss, leaving ~95 % attributable to reputational damage.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist (self-assessment)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Parallel trends testable & passes? .............. 0.8  
2. No anticipatory effects? ........................ 0.7  
3. No spillovers / SUTVA? .......................... 0.8  
4. Reliable measurement of treatment timing? ....... 0.9  
5. Sufficient power / sample size? ................. 1.0  

(Mean validity score ≈ 0.84: research design is strong but not bullet-proof.)

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
